# swarmops ref delete

Delete ref NAME.

```yaml
title: "swarmops ref delete"
description: "Delete ref NAME."
group: "refs"
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
mcp_tool: "ref_delete"
envelope_op: "ref_delete"
exit_codes: [0, 4, 5]
errors: [E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED, E_CAS_MISMATCH]
syntax: "swarmops ref delete [OPTIONS] --expect <REV> <NAME>"
```

## Syntax

```text
swarmops ref delete [OPTIONS] --expect <REV> <NAME>
```

## Required arguments

### `NAME`

Syntax: `<NAME>`.

The ref.

### `--expect`

Syntax: `--expect <REV>`.

The changeset the ref holds now.

Give the full changeset id you read (from ref list, show, log or a commit's result). A ref name or a relative revision such as main\~1 is read from the store when the command runs instead of pinning the id you read: the ref's own name always matches (a deleted ref errors instead), so the compare-and-swap protects nothing, and main\~1 on main never matches. An id prefix pins the id you read only until another changeset shares it; then it is E\_AMBIGUOUS\_ID.

After E\_CAS\_MISMATCH, the ref holds the error's `actual`, which someone else moved it to: look at it (swarmops show &lt;actual&gt;) before you delete it with --expect &lt;actual&gt;.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

## Examples

### CLI

```sh
swarmops --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17 ref delete release/1.0 --expect [c1]
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "op": "ref_delete",
  "api": 1,
  "result": {
    "name": "release/1.0",
    "old": "[c1]",
    "already_applied": false
  },
  "meta": {
    "repo": "[tmp]/store",
    "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
    "resolved": {
      "[c1]": "[c1]"
    },
    "auth": "trust"
  }
}
```

Exit code 0. Recorded by the CLI tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time.

## Return information

`result` is a `RefSetResp` (`swarmops schema RefSetResp` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `already_applied` | `boolean` | yes | The ref was already in the requested state, so nothing changed and a replay is safe; `old` and `new` are then the request's `expected_old` and `new`, resolved to full ids. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | The ref. |
| `new` | `string or null` | no | Its target after; omitted when the ref was deleted. |
| `old` | `string or null` | no | What the ref held before a move that was applied. On a replay (`already_applied`) it is `expected_old` as resolved, which the ref need not have held; omitted when `create` was given. |
| `warnings` | `array of string` | no | Problems found after the move became durable, such as failed housekeeping; the move itself succeeded. Omitted when empty. |

Envelope `op`: `ref_delete`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
- `4`: The operation can succeed when it is run again.
- `5`: An identity or policy requirement refused the operation.

## Errors

- [`E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#e_identity_required) (exit 5): A mutation was asked for without an identity.
- [`E_CAS_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#e_cas_mismatch) (exit 4): The ref no longer holds the expected target (or, with `create`, exists at another one); `details.actual` holds what it does, `null` when the ref does not exist.

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
